title: CHIRP: independent confidential human-factors reporting in aviation and maritime safety
summary: CHIRP is encoded as an independent confidential reporting route for aviation and maritime human-factors / just-culture concerns, especially when ordinary employer or regulator reporting feels unavailable or unsafe to the reporter.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0007 as a source-infrastructure record for the near-miss / signal-capture lane.

claims.claim: CHIRP describes itself as an independent and impartial charity improving safety in the air and at sea through a confidential human-factors incident reporting system that lets maritime and aviation workers share concerns without fear of being identified, with follow-up to relevant organisations when reporters agree.
what_would_change_status: CHIRP changes status, scope, or operating model.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: The UK CAA presents CHIRP as an independent confidential reporting route for aviation employees who feel unable to report safety concerns to their employer or the CAA, while warning that mandatory accident and occurrence reporting responsibilities still apply.
what_would_change_status: CAA changes CHIRP relationship or reporting obligations.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

claims.claim: The UK CAA says CHIRP is primarily concerned with human-factors and just-culture/reporting-culture issues, including skills, training, rules, equipment design/use, communication, workplace, manpower, organisation, and management.
what_would_change_status: CAA or CHIRP narrows/expands the reported issue taxonomy.

evidence_migration.note: rev0016 removes overloaded source_support.source_id/record_id keys and uses typed evidence_refs with ref_kind and support_role.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass official/institutional HTML extraction; no outcome evaluation or database sampling yet
limitations: This record establishes infrastructure existence, stated purpose, and reported process; it does not estimate effectiveness, representativeness, underreporting, or downstream safety impact.
No reporter narratives are imported in rev0007; privacy and de-identification boundaries are preserved.

type_payload.jurisdiction_or_scope: UK aviation and maritime sectors; CAA page describes UK airspace aviation context
reporter_protection_design: independence from direct employer reporting route
outputs: follow-up with relevant organisations when agreed
limitations: not a substitute for legally mandatory accident/occurrence reporting
effectiveness and closure outcomes not extracted
type_payload.query_value: Captures a non-US, human-factors-oriented signal route where the design problem is psychological and institutional safety to speak.

handling_notes: Do not attempt to re-identify reporters or named parties from confidential/de-identified reporting systems.
Infrastructure records are not evidence that all weak signals were handled well or that a reporting system prevented a specific accident.
Preserve distinction among mandatory reporting, voluntary self-reporting, confidential concern reporting, accident investigation, and recommendation tracking.

unknowns: Quantitative uptake, underreporting, signal quality, follow-through rates, and confidentiality failure history are not extracted yet.
No sample of individual reports, alerts, recommendations, or closed actions has been coded yet.
next_actions: Add database/export sampling plan and legal/ethical handling rules before importing any de-identified report narratives.
Add outcome or follow-through records showing when a report led to action, when it did not, and when confidentiality or reporting incentives failed.
Cross-link with warning-governance cases only when a source shows a specific relation; do not infer relation from infrastructure existence.
